full_judgment:
6. Plaintiff's case in nutshell is that the suit land was originally belonged to Pakistan Tobacco Company Ltd. After liberation of Bangladesh as per provision of President Order No. 16 of 1972 suit land vested in the Government. Government sold the suit land to the plaintiff by registered deed, Exhibit-1. Government sold to plaintiff 0.3550 acres of land from PS plot No. 17, 0.2287 acres of land from PS plot No. 18 and 0.2200 acres of land from PS Plot No. 19 of PS Khatian No.5 of J/L No.4 of mouza Kashim Bazar, PS Kotwali, District Chittagong. On behalf of Government Hon'ble President of Bangladesh executed the deed and after purchase plaintiff mutated its name, paying rents and maintaining possession. 

 7. Mrs Sigma Huda, learned Advocate, appearing for the appellant, filed application under Order XXIII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure for withdrawal of the suit stating that the suit is running with some formal defects and further submits that suit was filed on wrong recording of BS Khatian No. 63 and 64 but submits that, by this, authority has corrected the Khatian in favour of plaintiff appellant and further submits that while drafting the plaint it was mistake of the learned Advocate who did not include the land of PS plot No. 19 containing 0.2200 acres of land and learned Judge dismissed the suit holding that plaintiff claimed excess land than acquired by exhibit-1. Learned Advocate further submits that the genially of acquiring title by the plaintiff title by the plaintiff has not been properly described in the plaint, also the cause of action and schedule of the property have not been mentioned properly as there is no boundary of the schedule given in the plaint, as such, learned Advocate, further submits that if the suit running with this plaint the suit must fail as such prayed for withdrawal of the suit. 

 10. On considering the entire material before us as regard title of the plaintiff appellant as well as purchase from plaintiff appellant by added respondent Nos. 11-14 it is our considered vies that such purchase cannot be questioned as they acquired good title as per provision of President Order No.16 of 1972 because when the property vested in the Government it vested with its entirety free from any encumbrances as such, title of added respondent Nos. 11-14 is perfect title. It appears that plaintiff appellant sold the suit land to respondents Nos. 11-14 then delivered possession to respondents Nos. 11-14 who possessed the suit land unless the possession of the respondent Nos. 11-14 be in danger, a suit for permanent injunction by the seller plaintiff against defendant No. 1 without properly constituted the suit, without describing the schedule property and without describing properly cause of action is running with formal defect. It appears that defendant Nos. 4-8 claimed purchase from defendant No.1 whom authority found while correcting record of right of BS Khatian to be a fictitious person, did not admit that he sold land defendant Nos. 4-8 and also to defendant Nos. 9 and 10, as such, defendant Nos. 4-8 and 9 and 10 acquired no good title save and except dispute, as such, they should, at first, perfected their legal status before dispute possession of plaintiff to that effect, of respondent Nos. 11-14. It appears that plaintiff appellant sold the suit land to respondent Nos. 11-14 who has been delivered possession to respondent Nos. 11-14 and possessed the suit land, as such, unless the possession of the respondent Nos. 11-14 be in danger, a suit for permanent injunction by the seller plaintiff without any properly constituted and without describing properly cause of action is running, with formal defect.
